title: endue bridge v0: db
description: Database sessions (ADR 0281): PostgreSQL sessions the core opens, scoped by db:connect hosts. A session belongs to the caller that opened it: its notices, notifications, parameter changes and end arrive as db.* events, to that caller alone.

DbOpenRequest.description: Open a database session and sign in. The scope and the grant are checked before anything connects.

engine.description: The database engine; postgresql is the one the core speaks, any other is unsupported.

host.description: A host name or an IPv4 address, as net.connect takes it.

password.description: Used once for the sign-in and dropped. Without it the core reads the person's password file.

settings.description: Startup parameters (DateStyle, TimeZone, search_path, statement_timeout, application_name, ...). client_encoding, user, database and replication are invalid_params.

timeoutMs.description: How long the connection and the sign-in may take; 10000 by default.

ca.description: The authorities to trust, PEM; else the system's trust store. With require, the chain is checked too.

cert.description: The client's certificate, PEM, with any intermediates its authority needs; presented when the server asks for one (disable ignores it). Needs key.

key.description: The private key of cert, PEM: PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1, or PKCS#8 encrypted with PBES2 (keyPassword). Decoded before anything connects, held for the session and its cancel requests, never kept. Needs cert.

keyPassword.description: The passphrase of an encrypted key: used once to decrypt it and dropped.

DbSsh.description: An SSH tunnel the session goes through (ADR 0359): one SSH connection for the session and its cancel requests, opened before it and closed with it, through jump first when given. Every stream is a channel inside the core; nothing listens on a port. Exactly one of keyFile, agent, password and passwordRef signs in. db:connect must cover the SSH host and the jump host with their ports, as well as the database's host and port, which the SSH server connects to.

host.description: The SSH server, a host name or an IPv4 address.

user.description: Who signs in on the SSH server.

keyFile.description: The private key to sign in with, a full path (or ~/...) the core reads itself: OpenSSH, PEM or PKCS#8, Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA. Its content never crosses the bridge.

keyPassword.description: The passphrase of an encrypted keyFile: used once to decrypt it and dropped.

agent.description: Sign in with the keys the person's SSH agent holds.

password.description: The SSH password: used once for the sign-in and dropped.

DbSshHop.description: A jump host the tunnel reaches its SSH host through; it signs in as the SSH host does.

host.description: The SSH server, a host name or an IPv4 address.

user.description: Who signs in on the SSH server.

keyFile.description: The private key to sign in with, a full path (or ~/...) the core reads itself: OpenSSH, PEM or PKCS#8, Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA. Its content never crosses the bridge.

keyPassword.description: The passphrase of an encrypted keyFile: used once to decrypt it and dropped.

agent.description: Sign in with the keys the person's SSH agent holds.

password.description: The SSH password: used once for the sign-in and dropped.

DbSshFingerprint.description: An SSH host key's SHA-256 fingerprint, as OpenSSH prints it. In db.open, the one the person accepted for a host the caller has not trusted yet; it is kept once the tunnel opens.

DbSshAnswer.description: Why the tunnel did not open; nothing connected past hop. stage: connect (the SSH server could not be reached), hostKey (its key is not trusted: hostKey says why), auth (the sign-in was refused, or keyPassword or needsPassword says what is missing), forward (the SSH server could not reach the next hop or the database).

message.description: What failed, in words, naming the hop.

DbSshHopName.description: Which hop: the jump host, or the SSH host the database is reached from.

DbSshStage.description: Where the hop failed: connect, hostKey, auth or forward.

DbSshHostKeyStatus.description: unknown: not trusted yet. changed: differs from the trusted one.

DbSshHostKey.description: The key the SSH server presented. unknown: the caller trusts none for this host and port and none was accepted (show fingerprint, then open again with hostKey). changed: it differs from the trusted one (known), and is refused until db.hostKeys.delete forgets that one.

DbHostKeysDeleteRequest.description: Forget the SSH host key the caller trusts for a host and port, so the next db.open through it asks again. Forgetting one that is not trusted is not an error.

DbTlsMode.description: disable: plain TCP. prefer (the default): TLS when the server has it. require: TLS, the certificate not checked. verify-ca: the chain. verify-full: the chain and the host name.

DbOpenResult.description: Result of db.open: the session, signed in; or the server's refusal (error) and no session; or ssh when its tunnel did not open; or keyPassword when the client key cannot be decrypted; or needsPassword when no password was given, none was found in the password file or kept under passwordRef for the session's host, port and user, and the server asks for one.

pid.description: The server process of the session.

parameters.description: Every ParameterStatus the server sent (server_version, TimeZone, IntervalStyle, ...).

DbKeyPassword.description: tls.key is encrypted and keyPassword was not given (needed) or does not decrypt it (wrong); nothing connected.

DbTlsInfo.description: The TLS the session runs over.

DbSessionId.description: A session db.open opened, unique for the core's life.

DbRunRequest.description: Run one statement on a session and answer its first page. An earlier result with pages left is closed first.

sql.description: One statement; two are the server's 42601.

paramTypes.description: The parameters' type OIDs; 0, or a missing one, is the server's inference.

pageRows.description: Rows a page holds: 1000 by default.

pageBytes.description: Bytes of values a page holds: 4 MiB by default. A page holds one row even when it is larger.

DbRunResult.description: Result of db.run: the statement's first page.

DbScriptRequest.description: Run several statements on a session in one call, in order, each as db.run runs one, and answer each one's first page. It stops after a statement whose page has more (its rest is read with db.fetch, its COPY FROM STDIN fed with db.copy), at the first error unless goOn, and at a cancel; a transaction the statements open stays the session's.

statements.description: The statements, in the order they run.

goOn.description: Run on past a statement's error instead of stopping there.

pageRows.description: Rows each statement's first page holds: 1000 by default.

pageBytes.description: Bytes of values each statement's first page holds: 4 MiB by default. A page holds one row even when it is larger.

DbScriptStatement.description: One statement of db.script and its parameters, as db.run takes them.

sql.description: One statement; two are the server's 42601.

paramTypes.description: The parameters' type OIDs; 0, or a missing one, is the server's inference.

DbScriptResult.description: Result of db.script: one first page for each statement that ran, in order, each with its own notices. Fewer pages than statements: the last page has more, or an error, or the script was cancelled (cancelled), or a failure stopped it (failure, which belongs to the statement after the last page).

cancelled.description: A db.cancel came while the script ran: no statement after the last page started.

failure.description: What stopped the script that is not the server's error, as db.run would have failed with it: the statement after the last page did not answer; the session may be gone (io_error).

DbDescribeRequest.description: Ask the server what one statement takes and answers without running it: Parse and Describe of the unnamed statement, then Sync. Nothing executes, so it changes nothing and works on a read-only session; an earlier result with pages left is closed first.

sql.description: One statement; two are the server's 42601.

paramTypes.description: The parameters' type OIDs; 0, or a missing one, is the server's inference.

DbDescribeResult.description: Result of db.describe: the parameters' types (ParameterDescription) and the columns the statement answers (RowDescription; absent for NoData), or the server's error with its position, and the transaction state after it.

paramTypes.description: The type OID of $1, $2, ..., as the server infers them; empty with an error.

notices.description: The notices the server sent while this call ran.

DbFetchRequest.description: The next page of the session's open result, or close it without reading on.

pageRows.description: Rows a page holds: 1000 by default.

pageBytes.description: Bytes of values a page holds: 4 MiB by default. A page holds one row even when it is larger.

close.description: End the result without reading on.

DbFetchResult.description: Result of db.fetch: the next page, or an empty last one after close.

DbCopyRequest.description: Send data to the session's COPY ... FROM STDIN, or end it.

DbCopyParams.description: Parameters of db.copy: data, done and fail may come together; done or fail ends the COPY.

data.description: Up to 1 MiB of the COPY's bytes.

fail.description: Fail the COPY with this message (CopyFail).

DbCopyResult.description: Result of db.copy: more while the COPY waits for data, the statement's last page once it ends.

DbCancelRequest.description: Ask the server to cancel the statement the session runs; nothing when none runs. The statement's own answer then carries 57014.

DbCancelResult.description: Result of db.cancel: the request was sent.

DbCloseRequest.description: End a session. Closing one that already ended is not an error.

DbListRequest.description: The caller's sessions, as a frame that slept finds them again.

more.description: A result has pages left, or a COPY FROM STDIN waits for data.

DbPasswordName.description: A password the caller kept with db.passwords.set, by the name it chose (ADR 0311). db.open's passwordRef names it: the core reads the OS keychain itself, after the password file, and only for the host, port and user it was kept for; a name that is not kept, or was kept for another server or user, is as if none was given. Not with password.

DbPasswordsSetRequest.description: Keep a password in the OS keychain under a name, for one host, port and user; it is never answered back.

DbPasswordsSetParams.description: Parameters of db.passwords.set. A name already kept is replaced. A plugin's manifest must declare db:connect for the host and port; no grant is needed, since using it is db.open's.

host.description: The host db.open names, as net.connect takes it.

DbPasswordsDeleteRequest.description: Forget a password the caller kept: its keychain entry goes. Forgetting one that is not kept is not an error.

DbPasswordsListRequest.description: The passwords the caller kept: what each is kept for, never the password.

DbKeptPassword.description: A password the caller kept: its name and the host, port and user it is for.

DbPage.description: One page of a statement's answer. The first page has the columns; the last has the tag, the row count and the transaction state, or the server's error.

more.description: Exact: db.fetch has another page, or the COPY FROM STDIN waits for data.

tag.description: The command tag, counting every page.

rowCount.description: Rows over all pages, or the tag's count.

notices.description: The notices the server sent while this call ran, in the order it sent them: a statement's are on the pages of its db.run, db.fetch and db.copy, never also a db.notice event (each also came as a db.call.notice while the call ran). At most 10,000 a page.

noticesSkipped.description: Notices past the 10,000 a page keeps, counted and left out.

call.description: The session's number for the call this page answers, counting from 1: a db.call.notice with this number or a lower one is already on a page.

DbRow.description: One row: each value the server's text, or null.

DbValue.description: A value as the server prints it, or null for NULL.

DbColumn.description: One column, as RowDescription describes it.

tableOid.description: The table it comes from; 0 for an expression.

columnNumber.description: Its attribute number in that table; 0 for an expression.

DbCopy.description: A COPY's direction, format and number of columns.

DbCopyDirection.description: in: FROM STDIN. out: TO STDOUT.

DbServerError.description: An error or a notice the server sent, every field by name; positions are numbers.

severity.description: V, never localized (S on a server that sends no V).

other.description: Fields a later server adds, by their code.

DbNoticeEvent.description: A notice the server sent outside any call (with the sign-in, or while the session is idle). One sent while a call runs comes with that call's page instead.

DbCallNoticeEvent.description: A notice the server sent while a call runs, sent as it arrives, so a long statement's progress can be shown before its answer. The call's page carries it too, and the page is the record (ADR 0334, ADR 0358): an event whose call is already answered is late. At most the 10,000 a page keeps.

call.description: The number of the call that heard it, as that call's pages say (DbPage.call).

DbNotificationEvent.description: A NOTIFY on a channel the session listens to, also while it is idle.

DbParameterEvent.description: A run parameter the server reported changed (ParameterStatus).

DbClosedEvent.description: A session ended: the session's last event.

message.description: Why, when the network or the encoding ended it.

DbClosedReason.description: closed: db.close. server: the server ended it, with its FATAL error when it sent one. io: the network failed. encoding: the server's client_encoding stopped being UTF8. unloaded: its plugin stopped. revoked: the grant that covers it went. desk: the desk let it go.
